feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. (1) Iteration 1 (±3 cm, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg) is the best evidence so far: line losses fell from 1-2 to 1 per run, but every run still went off track at 11-16% progress with max_error 0.061-0.066 m (entityR2B). (2) Iteration 2 (±6 cm, 16 mm footprints, 3 cm lead) reached 0 line losses on every track, yet still went off track at max_error about 0.06 m, and s-bend progress fell to 4%. So the robot can leave the line while the sensors still see tape, and a wider footprint did not help. Oscillation stayed in 0.065-0.155 in all iterations, so jitter is not the limit. (3) The Integrator has kept the controller on the same weight pattern and kp 3.0 across iterations 1-3, so geometry changes alone have been tested without gain changes. Next race: if progress rises above 0.15 on the s-bend and max_error falls below 0.06 m with 0 line losses, keep the 2 cm lead and test sensor_size 0.012 at ±4 cm. If progress falls or line losses rise, restore the 4 cm lead and test sensor_size 0.016 alone. If line losses stay at 1 per run with the lead unchanged, a wider footprint or a ±4 cm span is the next candidate.
requested_changes: Keep the ±3 cm span, 5 sensors, and 12 mm footprints from iteration 1, and move the lead from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.02 m. Iteration 1 showed line losses at 1 per run with off-track exits at max_error about 0.06 m, so the lead is the single variable still untested below 3 cm.

If progress does not rise above 0.15 on the s-bend, restore y = 0.04 m and set sensor_size to 0.016 m alone. Iteration 2 used 16 mm footprints with a ±6 cm span and gave 0 line losses but no progress gain (score 26.99), so test footprint without changing span.

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.15 after the lead change, keep the lead and reduce kd or change sensor pitch rather than widening the span further. Iteration 2 kept oscillation at 0.065-0.075 on the oval and slalom, so high jitter would point to the lead.
